headline: St. Lucie County Detective Tyler Horstman Arrested on Felony DUI Charge
teaser: St. Lucie County Detective Tyler Horstman turned himself in Monday on a felony DUI warrant tied to a March 2 crash in Vero Beach involving an agency vehicle, Sheriff Richard Del Toro Jr. said.
body:
ST. LUCIE COUNTY — Detective Tyler Horstman of the St. Lucie County Sheriff's Office turned himself in at the Indian River County Jail on Monday, Oct. 26, after a felony DUI arrest warrant was issued in connection with an off-duty crash in Vero Beach, Sheriff Richard Del Toro Jr. announced.

Horstman was driving a sheriff's office vehicle when the crash occurred March 2, 2026, according to Del Toro. The Vero Beach Police Department took responsibility for the criminal investigation. The warrant issued Oct. 26 involves a DUI allegation with a blood or breath alcohol level of 0.15 or higher and serious personal injury, the sheriff said.

Del Toro said the sheriff's office learned Sept. 9 that blood testing indicated Horstman had a blood-alcohol concentration of 0.246. The sheriff said he immediately authorized an administrative investigation, and Horstman was placed on paid administrative leave Sept. 15.

After the felony warrant was issued, Horstman surrendered at the Indian River County Jail and was placed on unpaid administrative leave under agency policy, Del Toro said. The Vero Beach Police Department remains the lead agency in the criminal investigation. The sheriff's office has paused its internal investigation pending the outcome of the criminal proceedings.

Del Toro said the allegations raise concerns for the community and the agency, which holds its personnel to high standards both on and off duty. “Our responsibility to uphold the law comes with an expectation that we follow it ourselves,” he said. “When an employee is accused of violating that responsibility, we must address it fairly and hold them accountable through the appropriate process.”

The charge is an allegation. Horstman's guilt or innocence has not been determined in court.
